source.title: Electrical Power Corrosion Monitoring Market to Reach USD 115.29 Million by 2034 as Power Plant Asset Monitoring Gains Importance
source.body:
Global Electrical Power Corrosion Monitoring Market is represented by an analyst-derived market scenario of USD 81.00 million in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 84.24 million in 2026. According to Energy Resources Insights, the market is projected to reach USD 115.29 million by 2034, reflecting an assumed compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.0% during 2026–2034. Growing requirements for equipment integrity, maintenance planning, corrosion detection and operational reliability are supporting interest in specialized corrosion monitoring technologies.

https://www.energyresourcesinsights.com/electrical-power-corrosion-monitoring-market-694

Electrical power corrosion monitoring involves technologies used to identify, measure and track metal degradation in electricity generation equipment. The market includes corrosion sensors and probes, monitoring instruments, data acquisition hardware, corrosion analytics and related services. Applications include boilers and steam systems, cooling and water circuits, turbines and balance-of-plant equipment. These technologies help operators evaluate corrosion conditions and support maintenance decisions. The report's quantified market estimate uses a narrow coal-generation monitoring proxy rather than claiming coverage of every power-generation technology or electricity network asset.

Market at a Glance

·         2025 market size: USD 81.00 million

·         2026 estimate: USD 84.24 million

·         2034 forecast: USD 115.29 million

·         Forecast CAGR: 4.0% during 2026–2034

·         Leading region: Asia-Pacific, based on the analyst scenario

·         Leading type: Corrosion Sensors and Probes, based on qualitative assessment

·         Leading application: Boilers and Steam Systems, based on qualitative assessment

Equipment Reliability and Digital Monitoring Support Growth

Corrosion can affect the operational performance and service life of equipment used in electricity generation facilities. Boilers, steam circuits, cooling systems and other metallic components operate under conditions that can contribute to material degradation. Corrosion-specific monitoring technologies help operators observe these conditions and identify potential maintenance requirements.

The growing importance of predictive and condition-based maintenance is another factor supporting market opportunities. Power generation companies are increasingly interested in obtaining better information about equipment conditions between scheduled maintenance activities. Sensors, probes and connected data acquisition systems can provide measurements that help maintenance teams assess corrosion-related risks.

Boilers and steam systems represent an important application area because operating temperatures, water chemistry and material conditions can influence corrosion behavior. Monitoring solutions can help operators evaluate degradation in steam-generating equipment and associated water circuits.

Continuous online monitoring offers additional opportunities where operators require regular measurements and timely information. These systems can be integrated with plant monitoring infrastructure to improve visibility into equipment conditions. Periodic instrumented monitoring remains relevant where permanent installation is not economically justified or where degradation progresses more slowly.

However, corrosion monitoring requirements vary according to asset age, operating conditions, metallurgy, chemistry and maintenance practices. Equipment designed for general industrial applications cannot automatically be considered suitable for every power-generation environment.

Key Market Drivers and Challenges

Several factors are shaping the industry's outlook:

·         Power plant asset integrity: Monitoring technologies help operators evaluate corrosion-related degradation in critical generating equipment.

·         Maintenance modernization: Digital monitoring supports improved visibility into equipment conditions and maintenance planning.

·         Boiler and steam-system monitoring: High-temperature operating environments create requirements for corrosion-specific measurement solutions.

·         Continuous monitoring adoption: Connected sensors and data acquisition technologies provide more frequent information about equipment conditions.

·         Equipment life-extension programs: Operators maintaining existing generating assets may consider monitoring upgrades as part of broader reliability initiatives.

The market also faces challenges. Corrosion monitoring systems must demonstrate reliability under demanding operating conditions. Installation and calibration requirements, sensor compatibility and the interpretation of measurement data can affect procurement decisions. Budget limitations and the availability of experienced technical personnel may also influence adoption.

Coal plant retirement and changing generation patterns represent additional uncertainties for the quantified market scenario. The published forecast should be understood as a narrow analytical proxy rather than an audited estimate of total corrosion monitoring revenue across all power-sector assets.

Segmentation and Regional Outlook

The market is segmented by monitoring equipment type, application, monitoring method and procurement category.

·         By type: Corrosion Sensors and Probes; Monitoring Instruments and Data Acquisition; Corrosion Analytics and Services.

·         By application: Boilers and Steam Systems; Cooling and Water Circuits; Turbines and Balance of Plant.

·         By monitoring method: Continuous Online Monitoring; Periodic Instrumented Monitoring.

·         By procurement: New Monitoring Installation; Replacement and Renewal.

Asia-Pacific represents the largest regional opportunity in the analyst scenario, supported by its substantial thermal power generation base and associated equipment maintenance requirements. China and India are relevant markets for monitoring technologies used in power-generation facilities.

North America offers opportunities through plant maintenance programs, equipment modernization and established industrial instrumentation capabilities. Europe is supported by requirements for equipment reliability, technical monitoring and operational performance. The Middle East & Africa and South America present additional opportunities through electricity generation infrastructure and asset maintenance activities.

The regional percentages are analyst assumptions within the narrow coal-generation proxy and should not be interpreted as audited regional sales shares.

Competitive Landscape

The competitive environment includes corrosion instrumentation manufacturers, monitoring technology providers, system integrators and specialist industrial measurement companies.

Key companies and organizations identified in the report include Emerson, Cosasco, Metrohm, Endress+Hauser, MOBILTEX, MISTRAS and MetriCorr. EPRI is also relevant as a research and technical validation organization, rather than a commercial equipment manufacturer.

Emerson and Cosasco provide corrosion measurement technologies, including instruments and probes that may have relevant power-generation applications. Metrohm and Endress+Hauser offer measurement solutions applicable to water and steam-cycle monitoring. Other participants provide remote monitoring and asset-integrity technologies for selected energy infrastructure applications.

Competitive differentiation depends on measurement reliability, material compatibility, temperature performance, installation support and integration with existing plant monitoring systems. The available evidence does not establish audited power-sector revenue shares or a definitive supplier ranking.
